outcome: sworn serve becomes the project's resident surface: started with no flags it discovers the project, lists releases and runs with their lifecycle states and a needs-you row, follows new runs as they appear, and reads the operator config by convention - one serve per project, started once, instead of one per run wired by hand.

exclude: hosted/portal features and any cross-project fleet view (single project root)
creating approvals or verdicts from the dashboard (the existing command facade's authority boundary is unchanged)
the run-side telemetry export move (a later release; serve stays a view)

acceptance.text: sworn serve with no flags in a project root serves every discoverable run and release: pinned by cockpit fixtures over a project tree with multiple journals, asserting the catalog lists them with lifecycle states without any --run or --journal.
A run started after serve is already up appears without restarting serve: pinned by a fixture that adds a journal to the project surface and observes the catalog refresh.

A needs-you view surfaces parked runs and open attentions across the project's runs, each row naming the run and the action: pinned by a projection fixture with one healthy, one parked, and one attention-holding run.

The operator config is read from .sworn/operator.json by convention when --operator-config is absent, with the explicit flag still winning: pinned by cmd/sworn serve-options fixtures over present, absent, and both cases.

constraints: The dashboard can still only observe and route journaled operator commands through the existing facade; no new authority.
Per-run serve (explicit --run --journal) remains valid and unchanged.

Evidence basis: parseServeOptions hard-requires --run and --journal (cmd/sworn/operator.go:128-137); operating a release currently means kill+relaunch serve per run - five cycles in one observed evening (sworn#196).
The e2e check is declared, not executed by a role (ADR 0010).
Check evidence belongs in the submission's checks field, never in files added to the repository.
